vectors.description: Metoprolol tartrate 1 mg/mL gamma irradiation: first-order dose constant.
vectors.published_expected_text: "The loss in metoprolol tartrate follows an exponential decay for both EB and γ irradiations."

our_recomputation.foundation_note: foundation recomputation (Python float64, numpy, 2026-11-14, R = N_A k_B = 8.31446261815324 J/(mol K)), not a published value

vectors.note: Least-squares dose constant (DERIVED in the note; the note does not state the fit form). Assert with the reproducing fit form only: the free-intercept value rounds to 0.083 and falls outside the 0.0005 tolerance. Log-linear OLS gives 0.08319 per kGy with a free intercept and 0.08233 per kGy with the intercept fixed at ln(1054.41); the intercept fixed at ln(1054.41) fit reproduces 0.082. About 0.10 to 0.13 per kGy for e-beam and about 0.007 per kGy with mannitol (MDS68).

vectors.description: Solid oral products at simulated GCR doses: the radiation term must stay negligible.
vectors.published_expected_text: "All samples show comparable degradation, revealing that GCR exposure does not facilitate the degradation of the drugs."

our_recomputation.statement: engine radiation term must predict < 0.01% loss at 1 Gy for solids

tolerance.basis: inequality: 1 - exp(-k_D * 1 Gy) < 1e-4 for every solid product in the formulary, central and upper-bound terms

vectors.note: Negative control for any radiation term (see also space-pharmacy.md V9).
